plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $3, I will bid exactly $3 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay that competing bid, which maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. With no history from prior rounds to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot game, I'll bid my true value of $24 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true whether opponents are truthful, aggressive, or conservative - since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, bidding your true value maximizes expected profit. With my value at $11, I should bid exactly $11 to ensure optimal outcomes: I win only when profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable.
